title: A Bias-Variance Decomposition for Ensembles over Multiple Synthetic Datasets
summary: Decomposes the error of a model averaged over several synthetic datasets into six terms and shows that only two of them shrink as more synthetic datasets are drawn, which explains why ensembling over synthetic data helps high-variance downstream models most and lets the benefit of many datasets be predicted from a run on two. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the four generators the theory is checked against on the California housing task, run from the synthcity implementations and reported across downstream learners at one, two, five and ten synthetic datasets.
evidence: appendix E.1 states the compared algorithms are DDPM, TVAE, CTGAN and synthpop on the California housing dataset, describing TVAE and CTGAN as a variational autoencoder and a GAN designed for tabular data, with implementations taken from the synthcity library; appendix D.4 records that DDPM, TVAE and CTGAN were run on a single GPU; Table S3 reports their mean squared error under 1-NN, 5-NN and MLP downstream models at one, two, five and ten synthetic datasets

title: HARMONIC: Harnessing LLMs for Tabular Data Synthesis and Privacy Protection
summary: Fine-tunes a language model for tabular synthesis on an instruction set built by nearest-neighbour retrieval, so the model learns the relationships between a row's columns rather than memorising the rows themselves, and pairs it with a disclosure metric that scores how far generated records sit from their closest real counterpart. TVAE is one of the generators the result is measured against across machine-learning efficacy and likelihood metrics, and CTGAN is credited in the related work for introducing the conditional generator and for the machine-learning-efficacy benchmarking protocol the paper's evaluation is positioned against.
evidence: the related-work section states that building on GANs, CTGAN introduces a conditional generator and adapts a variational autoencoder for tabular data as TVAE; the evaluation discussion names the MLE benchmarking system proposed by Xu et al. as the existing approach it argues beyond; the baselines paragraph describes TVAE as a state-of-the-art VAE-based method for tabular data generation and the results table reports it alongside SMOTE, CTAB, TabDDPM, TabSyn, GReaT and REaLTabFormer

title: Structured Evaluation of Synthetic Tabular Data
summary: Argues that synthetic-data evaluation is a scattered collection of metrics with no account of what each one is sensitive to, and builds a structured framework that separates a synthesizer's ability to model the data-generating process from its ability to reproduce the sample, testing the framework by evaluating eight synthesizers on three datasets. Four of those eight come from SDV — GaussianCopula, CopulaGAN, CTGAN and TVAE — with the copula-based and autoencoder-based entries attributed to Patki et al. and the GAN and VAE entries to Xu et al.
evidence: the experiment section states that eight methods are evaluated, PCC, synthpop, DDPM, GReaT, GaussianCopula, TVAE, CTGAN and CopulaGAN; the framework demonstration paragraph attributes the GAN-based, autoencoder-based and copula-based synthesizers to Xu et al. 2019 and Patki et al. 2016; the related-work section cites Xu et al. for the likelihood-test family of metrics and for the known difficulties deep synthesizers have with heterogeneous types and column dependency

title: DSF-GAN: DownStream Feedback Generative Adversarial Network
summary: Adds a downstream feedback loop to tabular GAN training: a predictor trained on the real data scores each batch of generated rows and its loss is folded into the generator objective, so the generator is pushed toward samples that are useful for the eventual task rather than only plausible. CTGAN is the base architecture the mechanism is built on and demonstrated with, its generator loss rewritten to carry the extra feedback term, and the experiments use that architecture throughout.
evidence: section 2 states the architecture is demonstrated using the Conditional Tabular GAN, gives its minimax objective, and then defines the new generator loss as that objective plus a weighted feedback loss term; section 3 states that the base GAN architecture presented in Xu et al. 2019 was used for the experiment across two datasets

title: Generating Accurate Synthetic Survival Data by Conditioning on Outcomes
summary: Generates survival data by turning the usual factorisation around: time-to-event and censoring indicator are sampled first from a Dirichlet process mixture fitted to the observed outcomes, and the covariates are then drawn conditioned on them, which keeps the synthetic risk structure faithful without requiring the generator to model censoring itself. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the conditional generators the framework is instantiated on, adapted so their conditioning input carries the sampled time and event, with CTGAN's generator described in the paper's own notation as the conditional adversarial case.
affiliations: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology
evidence: the method section states the approach offers flexibility since the conditional distribution can in principle be modelled with any conditional generator, and that the experiments consider TVAE, CTGAN, ADS-GAN, TabDDPM and LLMs; a following subsection headed CTGAN describes it as a conditional adversarial generator synthesizing data through G(u, c) and explains how it is adapted for survival data generation; the related-work section credits Xu et al. with the conditional tabular GAN for mixed continuous and categorical variables
